newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, Argentina oil firms in joint accord.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Argentina oil firms in joint accord.

text.p: Brazil's state-owned oil giant Petrobras and Argentina's YPF will sign an accord Wednesday, paving the way for a joint-venture between the companies, Brazil's Mines and Energy Ministry said.
Officials from the two companies were due to meet in Argentina to sign an agreement setting down the basic principles for the new firm, the ministry said in a statement.

The Petrobras-YPF venture, which will serve as a holding company, will act in the purchase and resale of liquid and gas fuels, transportation, warehousing and refining of petroleum and petrochemical products, the statement said.
Petrobras and YPF will each hold 50 percent of the new company which will also be involved in the import and export of petroleum products.
About $730 million has been earmarked for investment over the next few years and that sum will be raised by borrowing, the statement said.
The presidents of Petrobras and YPF were also due to sign an agreement creating the so-called Mega Project, 38 percent owned by YPF, 34 percent by Petrobras and 28 percent by Dow Chemical.

The $630 million project seeks to develop natural gas fields in Argentina's Neugina Basin with the construction of a liquid gas separation plant, a 375-mile (600-km) gas pipeline and a fractionating unit in the city of Bahia Blanca.
Once up and running within three years, the project will produce about 516,000 tonnes a year of ethane will be sold to Argentina's Petroquimica Bahia Blanca.
Approximately 615,000 tonnes of liquified petroleum gas and 188,000 tonnes of primary gasoline will be exported each year to Brazil, the statement said.
